q.s: Which Harappan site marks the northernmost boundary of the Indus Valley Civilisation?
q.x: Manda (Jammu) is the northern limit; Daimabad is the southern, Alamgirpur the eastern and Sutkagendor the western limit.

q.s: Which of the following Harappan sites is NOT correctly matched with the boundary it marks?
q.x: The eastern limit is Alamgirpur; Lothal is in Gujarat.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT known to the Harappans?
q.x: Harappans knew wells, drains and bows and arrows, but no coined money; trade was by barter.

q.s: Which of the following animals is NOT shown around the seated figure on the Pashupati seal?
q.x: The figure is ringed by an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros and a buffalo, with two deer below; no lion appears.

q.s: The Pashupati seal, made of steatite, was found at:
q.x: The Pashupati (proto-Shiva) seal comes from Mohenjodaro.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Harappan religion is correct?
o: No temple has been clearly identified at any Harappan site.
Harappan worship centred on Vedic gods such as Indra and Agni.
Religion completely dominated Harappan public life.
Large temples stood at the centre of every Harappan city.
q.x: No clear temple has been found; worship was nature- and fertility-oriented and religion was present but not dominant.

q.s: Fire altars suggesting a fire cult among the Harappans have been found at:
q.x: Fire altars were found at Kalibangan and Lothal.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT associated with Harappan ritual practice?
q.x: No temple has been identified at any Harappan site; the Great Bath, fire altars and yogic figures point to ritual practice.

q.s: In the Vedic age, the head of a Vaishya guild (gana) was called:
q.x: Vaishya guilds were headed by a Shreshthin; the Gramani was the village headman.

q.s: The first reference to money-lending, where the usurer is called 'kusidin', is found in the:
q.x: The Shatapatha Brahmana first mentions the usurer (kusidin).

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a part of the Prasthanatrayi of Vedanta?
q.x: The Prasthanatrayi is the Upanishads, the Brahma Sutra and the Bhagavad Gita.

q.s: The central teaching of the Upanishads is the identity of:
q.x: The Upanishads are anti-ritualistic and teach the unity of Atman and Brahman.

q.s: Which is regarded as the largest stupa in Andhra Pradesh and South India?
q.x: The Amaravati Mahachaitya is the largest stupa in AP and South India.

q.s: According to the Archaeological Survey of India, the largest and tallest excavated stupa in India is at:
q.x: Kesariya (Bihar), about 104 ft high, is the largest and tallest excavated stupa.

q.s: Under Ashoka's Pillar Edict IV, independent judicial powers were given to the:
q.x: Pillar Edict IV gave the rajukas independent judicial power and gave condemned prisoners three days' respite.

q.s: Which of Ashoka's edicts forbade the branding of cattle?
q.x: Pillar Edict V lists animal-protection rules, including the ban on branding cattle on certain days.

q.s: After the Third Buddhist Council, the missionary Mahadeva was sent to:
q.x: Mahadeva went to Mahishamandala; Yona Dhammarakkhita to Aparantaka, Mahadhammarakkhita to Maharattha, Majjhima to the Himalaya.

q.s: Which of the following missionary-region pairs after the Third Buddhist Council is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Yona Dhammarakkhita went to Aparantaka; Maharakkhita went to the Yona country.

q.s: Most of the coins issued by the Gupta rulers were made of:
q.x: The Guptas issued the largest number of gold coins (dinaras).

q.s: Which of the following Gupta coin types was NOT issued by Samudragupta?
q.x: The king-queen type, showing Chandragupta I and Kumaradevi, was issued by Chandragupta I.

q.s: The first inscriptional evidence of sati in India (510 CE) is found in the:
q.x: The Eran inscription of Bhanugupta (510 CE) records the sati of Goparaja's wife.

q.s: According to the Junagadh inscription of Skandagupta, the Sudarshana lake was repaired by the governor:
q.x: Governor Parnadatta (and his son Chakrapalita) repaired the Sudarshana lake.

q.s: The earliest land grants in India were made by the:
q.x: The Satavahanas in the Deccan made the earliest land grants, not the Mauryas.

q.s: Land grants made to Brahmanas, with tax exemption and administrative rights, were called:
q.x: Brahmadeya grants went to Brahmanas; devadana or devagrahara grants went to temples.

q.s: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-hien visited India during the reign of:
q.x: Fa-hien came c. 399-412 CE under Chandragupta II.

q.s: The travel account of Fa-hien is known as:
q.x: Fa-hien's account is the Fo-kwo-ki; Si-yu-ki is Hiuen Tsang's.

q.s: Jalaluddin Firoz Khalji crowned himself in 1290 at:
q.x: Distrusted by the Delhi nobles and people, he was crowned at Kilokhri and stayed there.

q.s: During Iltutmish's reign, the Mongols under Chengiz Khan reached the Indus (1221) in pursuit of:
q.x: They chased Jalaluddin Mangbarni of Khwarazm; Iltutmish refused him shelter and the Mongols turned back.

q.s: Which medieval historian described Muhammad bin Tughlaq as a 'mixture of opposites'?
q.x: Barani called him a mixture of opposites.

q.s: The Futuhat-i-Firoz Shahi was written by:
q.x: It is Firoz Tughlaq's own account; Barani wrote the Tarikh-i-Firoz Shahi.

q.s: Which Governor of Punjab, humiliated by Ibrahim Lodi, invited Babur to invade India?
q.x: Daulat Khan Lodi sent his son Dilawar Khan to invite Babur; Alam Khan was Ibrahim's uncle and a pretender.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Delhi Sultans and the Caliph is correct?
o: The Sultans named the Caliph in the khutba and on coins, but he had only moral authority.
The Caliph collected a share of the Sultanate's land revenue.
The Caliph exercised real administrative control over the Sultanate.
The Caliph appointed the wazirs of the Delhi Sultanate.
q.x: The Caliph's authority over the Sultanate was nominal and moral only.

q.s: In the Delhi Sultanate, the officer who governed an iqta or wilayat was the:
q.x: The wali or muqti governed the province; the village had the muqaddam, chaudhari and patwari.

q.s: The grazing tax 'charai' on milch cattle was introduced by:
q.x: Charai was an Alauddin Khalji tax; Firoz Tughlaq abolished it.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the four sharia taxes retained by Firoz Tughlaq?
q.x: Firoz kept kharaj, jizya, zakat and khams and abolished charai along with other cesses.

q.s: Tughlaqabad near Delhi was built by:
q.x: Ghiyasuddin Tughlaq built Tughlaqabad.

q.s: Which of the following monuments was NOT built during the Delhi Sultanate?
q.x: The Qila-i-Kuhna Mosque was built by Sher Shah Suri; the Moth ki Masjid is of Sikandar Lodi's reign.

q.s: The first true dome in India is found in the:
q.x: The Alai Darwaza (Alauddin Khalji) has the first true dome.

q.s: The first true arch in India is found in the tomb of:
q.x: Balban's tomb has the first true arch.

q.s: Abdur Razzaq, who visited the court of Deva Raya II in 1443, was the envoy of:
q.x: Abdur Razzaq was the Persian envoy of the Timurid Shah Rukh.

q.s: Which of the following travellers is NOT correctly matched with his place of origin?
q.x: Abdur Razzaq came from Persia as Shah Rukh's envoy.

q.s: The Babri Masjid at Ayodhya (1528) was built by Babur's commander:
q.x: Mir Baqi built the mosque at Ayodhya in 1528.

q.s: Which of the following monument-place pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Babur was finally buried at Bagh-e-Babur in Kabul.

q.s: The Peacock Throne made for Shah Jahan was carried away in 1739 by:
q.x: Nadir Shah carried off the Peacock Throne after sacking Delhi in 1739.

q.s: In the Mughal military system, the term 'chehra' referred to:
q.x: Chehra was the descriptive roll; dagh was the branding of horses; Akbar revived both.

q.s: The Mughal emperor's personal bodyguards were known as:
q.x: The walashahi were the emperor's bodyguards.

q.s: Which historian explained the decline of the Mughal Empire mainly as a 'jagirdari crisis'?
q.x: Satish Chandra stressed the jagirdari crisis: too few jagirs for too many nobles.

q.s: Which of the following historian-explanation pairs on Mughal decline is NOT correctly matched?
o: Francois Bernier - Spread of private property in land
M. Athar Ali - Enlarged nobility under Aurangzeb
q.x: Bernier stressed the absence of private property in land.

q.s: Among the Sayyid brothers of the later Mughal period, Husain Ali Khan held the post of:
q.x: Abdullah Khan was the Wazir and Husain Ali Khan the Mir Bakhshi.

q.s: By the grant of 1719 obtained through the Sayyid brothers, Peshwa Balaji Vishwanath secured:
o: The title of Raja of Satara
Chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas
q.x: The 1719 grant gave the Marathas chauth and sardeshmukhi of the six Deccan subas.

q.s: In Mughal India, the property under the control of a Hindu woman was known as:
q.x: Stridhana was the Hindu woman's own property; mehr was the Muslim woman's dower.

q.s: Who among the following was the fifth Sikh Guru?
q.x: Amar Das was 3rd, Arjan Dev 5th, Hargobind 6th and Tegh Bahadur 9th.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT among the first five Sikh Gurus?
q.x: Guru Hargobind was the sixth Guru.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Maharaja Duleep Singh is correct?
o: He was crowned in 1839, immediately after Ranjit Singh's death.
In 1887 he sought the help of Tsar Nicholas II.
The First Anglo-Sikh War of his reign ended with the Treaty of Lahore (1846).
He fought the British at the Battle of Plassey.
q.x: The war ended with the Treaty of Lahore; he was crowned in 1843 and approached Tsar Alexander III in 1887.

q.s: Maharaja Ranjit Singh was immediately succeeded in 1839 by:
q.x: Kharak Singh succeeded in 1839; Duleep Singh was crowned only in 1843.

q.s: Which Sikh Guru was executed in 1606 under Jahangir for helping Prince Khusrau?
q.x: Guru Arjan Dev, the first martyr Guru, was executed in 1606.

q.s: Guru Tegh Bahadur was executed at Chandni Chowk in 1675 on the orders of:
q.x: Aurangzeb had Guru Tegh Bahadur executed in 1675.

q.s: At Fatehpur Sikri, the debates among scholars of different religions were held in the:
q.x: Akbar built the Ibadat Khana (1575) for religious debates.

q.s: Which building at Fatehpur Sikri is noted for its single central carved pillar?
q.x: The Diwan-i-Khas has a single carved central pillar.

q.s: The white-marble tomb of Shaikh Salim Chishti stands in the courtyard of the Jama Masjid at:
q.x: Salim Chishti's tomb is in the Jama Masjid courtyard at Fatehpur Sikri.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT located at Fatehpur Sikri?
q.x: The Akbari Mahal is in Agra Fort; the other three are at Fatehpur Sikri.

q.s: The Tabaqat-i-Nasiri was written by:
q.x: Minhaj-us-Siraj wrote the Tabaqat-i-Nasiri; the Tabaqat-i-Akbari is by Nizamuddin Ahmad.

q.s: Which of the following work-author pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Muntakhab-ut-Tawarikh is by Abdul Qadir Badauni.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the origins of Bhakti is correct?
o: The Bhagavad Gita forms part of the Shanti Parva.
The word bhakti comes from the root 'bhaj', meaning to share or participate.
The Bhagavata Purana was composed in Bengal in the 12th century.
The Bhakti Yoga is the first chapter of the Bhagavad Gita.
q.x: Bhakti comes from 'bhaj'; the Gita is in the Bhishma Parva and the Bhagavata Purana is a southern text of the 9th-10th century.

q.s: The Bhagavad Gita forms part of which Parva of the Mahabharata?
q.x: The Gita is in the Bhishma Parva.

q.s: The Sri Bhashya, a commentary on the Brahma Sutra, was written by:
q.x: Ramanuja wrote the Sri Bhashya; Nimbarka wrote the Vedanta Parijata Saurabha.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of commentator and commentary on the Brahma Sutra is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The Sri Bhashya is Ramanuja's; Vallabha wrote the Anubhashya and Nimbarka the Vedanta Parijata Saurabha.

q.s: Aradhya Saivism, a moderate Virashaiva sect of Andhra, was founded by:
q.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya founded Aradhya Saivism, which kept Vedic learning and varna.

q.s: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote the Basava Puranam in which metre?
q.x: The Basava Puranam is in the dwipada metre.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a sepoy mutiny that preceded the Revolt of 1857?
q.x: The Santhal rising was a civil (tribal) revolt, not a rising of sepoys.

q.s: The Bengal Famine of 1770 occurred during the period of the:
q.x: The famine came under the Dual Government (1765-72), when the Company kept squeezing revenue; the others came later.

q.s: The Famine Code of 1883 was based on the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Strachey Commission (1878) studied famine policy and its findings formed the basis of the Famine Code.

q.s: Who is regarded as the pioneer of the labour movement in India?
q.x: N.M. Lokhande founded the Bombay Millhands' Association (1890), India's first labour organisation.

q.s: India's first trade union in the modern sense, the Madras Labour Union (1918), was founded by:
q.x: B.P. Wadia founded the Madras Labour Union in 1918.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Brahmo Samaj is correct?
o: It held the Vedas to be infallible.
It believed in the avatars of Vishnu.
It was a reform movement within Hinduism.
q.x: The Brahmo Samaj was a reform movement within Hinduism that denied the infallibility of the Vedas and rejected avatars.

q.s: In the 1937 elections in the Madras Presidency, the Justice Party was routed and a Congress ministry was formed under:
q.x: With no mass base and opposed to the freedom struggle, the Justice Party lost; Rajaji formed the ministry.

q.s: Who ran a widow asylum at Guntur from 1902?
q.x: Unnava Lakshmibayamma ran the Guntur widow asylum (1902).

q.s: 'Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala' was written by:
q.x: Bandaru Achamamba wrote Abala Sachcharitra Ratnamala; Seethamma wrote Ahalya Bai.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Madanapalle is correct?
o: Annie Besant founded the Besant (National) Theosophical College there in 1916.
Jiddu Krishnamurti was the first principal of the Besant Theosophical College there.
Tagore composed 'Jana Gana Mana' there in 1911.
Annie Besant set the tune of 'The Morning Song of India'.
q.x: Besant founded the college in 1916; James H. Cousins was its first principal and Margaret Cousins set the tune.

q.s: Rabindranath Tagore translated 'Jana Gana Mana' into English as 'The Morning Song of India' in 1919 at:
q.x: Tagore made the translation at Madanapalle in February 1919; Margaret Cousins set the tune.

q.s: In 1898, the office of the Nadwatul Ulama moved from Kanpur to:
q.x: The Nadwatul Ulama, decided upon at Kanpur in 1893, moved to Lucknow in 1898.

q.s: In 1876, the maximum age for the Indian Civil Service examination was reduced from 21 to:
q.x: The cut from 21 to 19 handicapped Indians and led to demands, e.g. from the Kakinada Literary Association, for a higher age limit.

q.s: The Bombay Presidency Association (1885) was founded by Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang and:
q.x: Its founders were Pherozeshah Mehta, K.T. Telang and Badruddin Tyabji.

q.s: Who was the President of Tilak's Indian Home Rule League?
q.x: Joseph Baptista was President and N.C. Kelkar Secretary of Tilak's league.

q.s: The organising secretary of Annie Besant's All India Home Rule League was:
q.x: George Arundale was the organising secretary of Besant's league.

q.s: Which of the following Congress session-president pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Jawaharlal Nehru presided at Lahore (1929), which adopted Purna Swaraj.

q.s: During the Civil Disobedience Movement, salt was made at Sanikatta in:
q.x: Sanikatta salt works were the centre of the movement in Karnataka.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of region and form of the Civil Disobedience Movement is NOT correctly matched?
o: Assam - Protest against the Cunningham Circular
Sholapur - Raid on the Dharasana salt works
q.x: Dharasana is in Gujarat; Sholapur saw a textile workers' rising and martial law.

q.s: Subhas Chandra Bose's book 'The Indian Struggle' was published in London in:
q.x: 'The Indian Struggle' was published in London in 1935.

q.s: Subhas Chandra Bose was born in 1897 at:
q.x: Bose was born at Cuttack on 23 January 1897.

q.s: The Land Reforms Bill that led to the Andhra Pradesh Land Ceiling Act of 1973 was brought under Chief Minister:
q.x: The ceiling bill was P.V. Narasimha Rao's; the Act was enforced from 1 January 1975.

q.s: Which law bars the transfer of land in the Scheduled Areas of Andhra Pradesh to non-tribals?
q.x: The AP Scheduled Areas Land Transfer Regulation 1/1959 protects tribal land.

q.s: The JVP Committee (1949) on linguistic states consisted of Jawaharlal Nehru, Vallabhbhai Patel and:
q.x: J-V-P stood for Jawaharlal, Vallabhbhai and Pattabhi; it advised postponing linguistic reorganisation.

q.s: The S.K. Dhar Commission (1948) preferred the reorganisation of states on the basis of:
q.x: The Dhar Commission rejected language as the sole basis and preferred administrative convenience.

q.s: Under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act, 2014, Polavaram was declared a national project by Section:
q.x: Section 90 declares Polavaram a national project.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of section of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014 and subject is NOT correctly matched?
o: Section 90 - Polavaram as a national project
Section 46 - Finance Commission award and backward-area package
q.x: Section 10 amends the First Schedule (entry 29, Telangana); the Act has no SCS section.

q.s: The Bhimbetka rock shelters, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2003, are in which district of Madhya Pradesh?
q.x: Bhimbetka lies in Raisen district.

q.s: The animal most commonly painted in the Bhimbetka rock shelters is the:
q.x: The deer is the most frequently painted animal at Bhimbetka.

q.s: Which Satavahana ruler restruck the silver coins of the Saka ruler Nahapana?
q.x: Gautamiputra Satakarni defeated Nahapana and restruck his coins (Jogalthembi hoard).

q.s: Which of the following statements about Satavahana coins is correct?
o: Portrait coins began with Gautamiputra Satakarni.
Most Satavahana coins were of gold.
Their bilingual coins used Prakrit and Greek.
The Ujjain symbol appears only on the obverse.
q.x: Portrait coins began with Gautamiputra; the bilingual coins use Prakrit and a Dravidian language, and the Ujjain symbol is on the reverse.

q.s: The doctrine of Syadvada belongs to which religion?
q.x: Syadvada is the Jain doctrine of 'maybe'; Kundakunda was a Jain teacher.

q.s: The Sunyavada (Madhyamika) doctrine of Buddhism was propounded by:
q.x: Acharya Nagarjuna propounded Sunyavada.

q.s: The Ikshvaku queen Rudradhara Bhattarika was the daughter of:
q.x: Rudradhara Bhattarika was the daughter of Rudrasena of Ujjain.

q.s: The Buddhist site of Nagarjunakonda was discovered in 1926 by:
q.x: A.R. Saraswati discovered it in 1926; Longhurst excavated it in 1927-31.

q.s: Which of the following year-work pairs at Nagarjunakonda is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: 1954-60 was the rescue excavation before submergence; the site was found in 1926.

q.s: Which Vishnukundin ruler built the Govinda Vihara at Chaitanyapuri (Hyderabad)?
q.x: Govinda Varma I built the Govinda Vihara; his queen built the Mahadevi Vihara.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched in Vishnukundin religious history?
o: Vikramendra Varma II - Irundhera grant to the Mahadevi Vihara
Madhava Varma II - Called the 'destroyer of Buddhism'
Kumarilabhatta - Builder of the Mahadevi Vihara
q.x: Kumarilabhatta is remembered for attacking Jainism, not for building viharas.

q.s: The first mention of Ghatikas in Andhra comes from the inscriptions of the Vishnukundin ruler:
q.x: Indrabhattaraka Varma's inscriptions first mention Ghatikas in Andhra.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Ghatikas of the Vishnukundin period is correct?
o: They were higher colleges of Sanskrit and Vedic learning.
Special Ghatikas functioned at Nagarjunakonda and Ghantasala.
They were colleges of Prakrit and Buddhist learning.
q.x: Ghatikas taught 14 vidyas; special Ghatikas were at Amaravati and Vengi.

q.s: The Aihole inscription of Pulakesin II, composed by Ravikirti, is dated:
q.x: The Aihole inscription dates from 634-35 CE.

q.s: Pulakesin II stopped Harsha's southward advance on the banks of the:
q.x: Harsha was checked on the Narmada c. 618-19.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Eastern Chalukya administration is correct?
o: The Grameyaka was a temple priest.
The Grameyaka or Urgavunda was the village head.
q.x: The Grameyaka was the village head; the Sthanadhipati managed temples and their endowments.

q.s: In the Eastern Chalukya kingdom, the 'Ashtadasa Tirthas' were:
q.x: The Ashtadasa Tirthas were the eighteen administrative offices, not bathing places.

q.s: Pakanadu of the Eastern Chalukya period corresponds to the present region of:
q.x: Pakanadu was Nellore; Palnadu was Macharla-Gurajala and Kammanadu Bapatla-Ongole.

q.s: Which of the following nadu-region pairs of the Eastern Chalukya period is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Venginadu was the Krishna-Godavari region.

q.s: Which Telugu poet was given the title 'Ubhayakavimitrudu'?
q.x: Tikkana was Ubhayakavimitrudu (also Kavibrahma); Nannaya was Vaganusasana.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of Telugu poet and title is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Ubhayakavimitrudu was Tikkana; Peddana was Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

q.s: The Reddi capital was shifted from Addanki to Kondavidu by:
q.x: The Manyapuram inscription records Anavota Reddi's shift of the capital to Kondavidu.

q.s: The Kondapalli hill fort in the Krishna region is credited to:
q.x: Kondapalli fort is credited to Prolaya Vema Reddi, founder of the Reddi kingdom.

q.s: The first European factory in Andhra was set up at Machilipatnam in 1605 by the:
q.x: The Dutch set up at Machilipatnam in 1605 under Muhammad Quli Qutb Shah; the English came in 1611.

q.s: The first Vijayanagara king to use cannon was:
q.x: Bukka I is credited with the first use of cannon in Vijayanagara.

q.s: The standing army of Vijayanagara was commanded by the:
q.x: The Siddha (standing) army was under the Dalavayi and was paid every four months.

q.s: After the fall of Warangal in 1323, Muhammad bin Tughlaq renamed it:
q.x: Warangal became Sultanpur, under Malik Burhanuddin with Malik Maqbul as deputy.

q.s: The first organised resistance to Muslim rule in Andhra after 1323 is known as the:
q.x: The Vimochanodyamam, led by the Musunuri Nayaks, was the first organised resistance.

q.s: Under the Kakatiyas, which Saiva sect provided anna dana (free food) at temples?
q.x: The Kalamukhas ran feeding houses and gave anna dana at Kakatiya temples.

q.s: In Vijayanagara temple architecture, the pillared hall meant for the divine marriage ceremony was the:
q.x: The kalyana mandapa was used for the celestial marriage of the deity.

q.s: The towering gateways of Vijayanagara temples that dwarfed the central shrine were called:
q.x: Raya gopurams were the huge gateway towers of the Vijayanagara style.

q.s: During the Revolt of 1857, the Diwan of Hyderabad who stayed loyal to the British was:
q.x: Salar Jung I and the Nizam kept Hyderabad loyal, limiting the revolt in the Deccan.

q.s: The Nizam of Hyderabad at the time of the Revolt of 1857 was:
q.x: Afzal-ud-Daula became Nizam in 1857 and stayed loyal to the British.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Sir Arthur Cotton is correct?
o: He built the Prakasam Barrage at Vijayawada.
On his suggestion Machilipatnam district was renamed Godavari.
q.x: He was called Apara Bhagiratha and Cotton Dora; he was knighted in 1861.

q.s: On Sir Arthur Cotton's suggestion, Rajahmundry district was renamed:
q.x: Rajahmundry district became Godavari and Machilipatnam district became Krishna.

q.s: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was repealed in 1882 by:
q.x: Passed under Lytton, the Act was repealed by Ripon in 1882.

q.s: The Adams Regulation restricting the press was issued in:
q.x: John Adams issued the licensing regulation in 1823.

q.s: The Andhra Sahitya Parishat was founded in 1911 at:
q.x: It was founded at Madras in 1911 and later moved to Kakinada.

q.s: Kokkonda Venkataratnam was known by the title:
q.x: He was called Andhra Bhasha Johnson as an orthodox Telugu scholar; Gadya Tikkana was Veeresalingam.

q.s: The Kooli Rakshana Samiti, formed in March 1935 to organise workers and farm labourers, was set up at:
q.x: The Kooli Rakshana Samiti was formed at Guntur in 1935.

q.s: The first political summer school of the socialists in Andhra (1937) was held at:
q.x: Kothapatnam (1937) hosted the first summer school; Hindupur hosted the 1938 one.

q.s: Who made the Telugu film 'Rythu Bidda' (1939), which reflected the anti-zamindari struggle?
q.x: Rythu Bidda (1939) was directed by Gudavalli Ramabrahmam.

q.s: Yakasiri Chellamma is remembered for leading women's chilli-powder resistance in the anti-zamindari struggle at:
q.x: She led women's resistance in the Nellore/Venkatagiri struggle.

q.s: The Andhra Mahila Sabha was founded at Madras in 1937 by:
q.x: Durgabai Deshmukh founded the Andhra Mahila Sabha at Madras for women's education and welfare.

q.s: Durgabai Deshmukh, a member of the Constituent Assembly, was awarded the Padma Vibhushan in:
q.x: She received the Padma Vibhushan in 1975.

q.s: Andhra Prakasika (1885), the first political weekly in Telugu, was started by:
q.x: A.P. Parthasarathi Naidu started Andhra Prakasika in 1885.

q.s: Which is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam?
q.x: Sugreeva Vijayam of Kandukuri Rudrakavi is the first published Telugu Yakshaganam.

q.s: The Telugu Yakshaganam was traditionally performed by the:
q.x: The Jakkula community performed Yakshaganam; Koravanji was its precursor.

q.s: Kolattam, a folk dance of Andhra Pradesh, is essentially a:
q.x: Kolattam is a group stick dance of 8 or 12 dancers led by a Pennadi.

q.s: Which of the following source-content pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Gargi Samhita - Yavana march on Pataliputra
Mahabhashya - Yavana siege of Saketa and Madhyamika
Divyavadana - Pushyamitra as a persecutor of Buddhists
q.x: Mudrarakshasa deals with Chandragupta Maurya's rise to power.

q.s: The Fourth Buddhist Council held under Kanishka was presided over by:
q.x: Vasumitra presided; Parshva urged Kanishka to hold the Council.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT associated with the court of Kanishka?
q.x: Kalidasa belongs to the Gupta age; Charaka was Kanishka's physician.

q.s: The Pala-period centres of learning such as Nalanda were destroyed around 1193-1200 by:
q.x: Bakhtiyar Khilji destroyed Nalanda (one tradition gives 1194) and other viharas.

q.s: In the WTO era, debt-linked farmer suicides in India were especially marked in:
q.x: Farmer distress and suicides were concentrated in Maharashtra and Andhra Pradesh.

q.s: The Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2009 rests on which Article of the Constitution?
q.x: The RTE Act gives effect to Article 21A (86th Amendment) and came into force in 2010.

q.s: Which of the following statements about forces of social change in India is correct?
o: Urbanisation turns the family into a production unit.
The Caste Disabilities Removal Act, 1850 protected inheritance on conversion.
The RTE Act, 2009 rests on Article 45.
q.x: Urbanisation makes the family a consumption unit and increases social distance; the RTE Act rests on Article 21A.

q.s: Which of the following books was written by M.N. Srinivas?
o: Religion and Society among the Coorgs
q.x: Srinivas wrote Religion and Society among the Coorgs; Ghurye wrote Caste and Race in India, Dumont Homo Hierarchicus.

q.s: Under Section 11 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a bigamous marriage is:
q.x: A bigamous marriage is void under Section 11; Section 12 deals with voidable marriages.

q.s: The custom in which a widow marries her deceased husband's brother is called:
q.x: Levirate (Devara Nyayam) is found among the Gond and Munda; sororate is marriage with the deceased wife's sister.

q.s: The concept of 'dominant caste' was given by:
q.x: M.N. Srinivas gave the concepts of dominant caste and Sanskritisation.

q.s: M.N. Srinivas developed the concept of dominant caste from his study of the village of:
q.x: He studied Rampura in Mysore; Shamirpet was S.C. Dube's village and Kishan Garhi McKim Marriott's.

q.s: 'Imagined Communities', a constructivist work on identity and nationalism, was written by:
q.x: Benedict Anderson wrote Imagined Communities; Barth wrote Ethnic Groups and Boundaries.

q.s: Clifford Geertz and Edward Shils are associated with which view of ethnic identity?
q.x: Geertz and Shils are primordialists; Paul Brass is an instrumentalist.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution directs the State to secure equal pay for equal work for both men and women?
q.x: Article 39(d) is the DPSP on equal pay for equal work.

q.s: Which of the following Article-content pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 39(d) - Equal pay for equal work
Article 51A(e) - Renounce practices derogatory to women
Article 15(3) - Special provisions for women and children
q.x: Article 44 deals with the Uniform Civil Code; monuments are under Article 49.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Article 17 of the Constitution is correct?
o: 'Untouchability' is defined in the Protection of Civil Rights Act, 1955.
State Legislatures can prescribe punishment for offences under Article 17.
Article 17 is one of the Directive Principles.
Article 17 abolishes untouchability and is part of the Right to Equality.
q.x: 'Untouchability' is not defined anywhere, and under Article 35(a)(ii) only Parliament can prescribe punishment.

q.s: The Tsundur massacre of Dalits (1991) took place in which district of Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Tsundur is in Guntur district.

q.s: Which of the following incident-place pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: Hathras is in Uttar Pradesh; Karamchedu sparked the independent Dalit movement in AP.

q.s: The special provisions for SCs, STs, BCs and Anglo-Indians (Articles 330-342A) are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
q.x: Articles 330-342A form Part XVI.

q.s: The proviso to Article 164(1), requiring a Minister in charge of tribal welfare, applies to all of the following States EXCEPT:
q.x: It covers Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh and Odisha; Bihar was dropped in 2006.

q.s: Which State's 2025 Bill was the first State law to define hate speech?
q.x: Karnataka's 2025 Bill defines hate speech and also makes organisations liable.

q.s: Which Report of the Law Commission (2017) dealt with defining hate speech?
q.x: The 267th Report (2017) dealt with hate speech.

q.s: Which State's 2019 Act was the first State law reserving 75% of private industrial jobs for locals?
q.x: Andhra Pradesh's 2019 Act came first; Haryana's followed in 2020.

q.s: Under Article 16(3), residence requirements for public employment can be prescribed only by:
q.x: Article 16(3) empowers only Parliament; Article 16(2) bars discrimination by place of birth or residence.

q.s: 'Dharya Sparsa - Operation Flush-Out' against drugs and illegal liquor in Andhra Pradesh was launched by the police of:
q.x: The Chittoor Police launched the operation.

q.s: The Justice J.S. Verma Committee, set up after the Nirbhaya case of December 2012, submitted its report in:
q.x: The Verma Committee reported in January 2013.

q.s: The direct legislative outcome of the Nirbhaya case was the:
o: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005
q.x: The Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 2013 followed the Verma Committee report.

q.s: Under the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015, children in need of care and protection are dealt with by the:
q.x: The Child Welfare Committee handles children in need of care; the JJ Board handles children in conflict with law.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Juvenile Justice Act, 2015 is correct?
o: Both social workers in a Juvenile Justice Board must be women.
Working children are treated as children in conflict with law.
A Child Welfare Committee has a Chairperson and four members.
Registration is compulsory only for government-run Child Care Institutions.
q.x: At least one JJB social worker must be a woman; working children need care and protection; all CCIs must register.

q.s: The Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015 came into force on:
q.x: It came into force on 15 January 2016, as a response to the 2012 Delhi case.

q.s: The 2021 amendment of the JJ Act made which officer the focal point for its implementation in a district?
q.x: The 2021 amendment (in force from 1 September 2022) empowered the District Magistrate.

q.s: According to the Tendulkar method, the poverty ratio in India in 2011-12 was:
q.x: Tendulkar poverty fell from 37.2% (2004-05) to 21.9% (2011-12).

q.s: Calorie norms of 2,400 (rural) and 2,100 (urban) were the basis of poverty estimates under the:
q.x: The calorie norms belong to the Alagh/Lakdawala method; Tendulkar moved away from calorie norms.

q.s: Pradhan Mantri Ujjwala Yojana is implemented by the Ministry of:
q.x: PMUY is run by the Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas.

q.s: Ujjwala 2.0, giving a free first refill and a hotplate, was launched in August 2021 at:
q.x: Ujjwala 2.0 was launched at Mahoba; the original scheme was launched at Ballia in 2016.

q.s: The Mid-Day Meal Scheme, as the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education, began on:
q.x: The scheme began on 15 August 1995.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Mid-Day Meal Scheme / PM POSHAN is correct?
o: It was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021.
Kerala was the first State to introduce the mid-day meal.
Its cost is shared between the Centre and the States in the ratio 75:25.
It began in 2001 on the orders of the Supreme Court.
q.x: It was renamed PM POSHAN in 2021; Tamil Nadu was the first State and costs are shared 60:40.

q.s: The PFRDA became the statutory regulator of the National Pension System under the PFRDA Act of:
q.x: The PFRDA Act was passed in 2013.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Pension System is correct?
o: PFRDA became its statutory regulator under the PFRDA Act, 2013.
From 2009 it was opened only to resident citizens.
It covered the armed forces from 1 January 2004.
q.x: The armed forces were excluded, and from 2009 it was opened to all citizens aged 18-70, including NRIs.

q.s: The Central Waqf Council, set up in 1964, is a:
q.x: It is a statutory body; the 2013 amendment enabled it to direct State Waqf Boards.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Waqf bodies is correct?
o: The Central Waqf Council is a constitutional body.
The Waqf (Amendment) Bill, 2024 was introduced in the Rajya Sabha.
The Waqf (Amendment) Act, 2013 enabled the Central Waqf Council to direct State Waqf Boards.
The Central Waqf Council was set up in 1995.
q.x: The Council is a statutory body of 1964; the 2024 Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha.

q.s: The National Institute for the Empowerment of Persons with Intellectual Disabilities (NIEPID) is located at:
q.x: NIEPID is at Secunderabad; the visual-disability institute is at Dehradun.

q.s: Which of the following national institute-location pairs is NOT correctly matched?
q.x: The locomotor-disability institute is at Kolkata.

q.s: BTIA, the agreement under negotiation between India and the EU since 2007, stands for:
o: Broad Treaty on Investment and Arbitration
q.x: BTIA is the Broad-based Trade and Investment Agreement.

q.s: The India-EU Trade and Technology Council was set up in:
q.x: The TTC was set up in 2022.

q.s: The Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO), founded on 16 October 1945, is headquartered at:
q.x: The FAO is at Rome; 16 October is World Food Day.

q.s: Which of the following UN bodies is NOT headquartered at Rome?
q.x: WHO is at Geneva; FAO, WFP and IFAD are Rome-based.

q.s: Which of the following land neighbours of India is NOT a member of SAARC?
q.x: SAARC includes every land neighbour of India except China and Myanmar.

q.s: How many member countries does SAARC have?
q.x: SAARC has eight members (Afghanistan joined in 2007).

q.s: India became a member of the Missile Technology Control Regime (MTCR) in:
q.x: India joined the MTCR in June 2016, Wassenaar in December 2017 and the Australia Group in January 2018.

q.s: India is a member of all of the following export control regimes EXCEPT the:
q.x: India is not an NSG member; it has only the 2008 India-specific waiver.

q.s: The Information Fusion Centre - Indian Ocean Region (IFC-IOR) was set up in December 2018 at:
q.x: IFC-IOR is at Gurugram, collocated with IMAC.

q.s: The Djibouti Code of Conduct (2009), to which India became an observer in 2020, deals with:
q.x: The IMO-backed Djibouti Code of Conduct is directed against piracy.

q.s: The President's ordinance-making power under Article 123 is modelled on which Section of the Government of India Act, 1935?
q.x: Section 42 gave the Governor-General ordinance power; hence Article 123 is called a relic of the 1935 Act.

q.s: The first formal demand for a Constituent Assembly was made at Ranchi in May 1934 by the:
q.x: The Swaraj Party made the demand in May 1934; the CWC adopted it in June 1934.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a member of the Cabinet Mission of 1946?
q.x: The Mission was Pethick-Lawrence, Cripps and A.V. Alexander; Wavell was the Viceroy.

q.s: Which of the following countries does NOT have a single written constitution?
q.x: The British constitution evolved through conventions, statutes and judicial decisions.

q.s: The Directive Principles of State Policy in the Indian Constitution were borrowed mainly from the Constitution of:
q.x: DPSPs come from Ireland; Fundamental Rights from the USA.

q.s: Which of the following pairs of constitutional feature and source is NOT correctly matched?
o: Structural part - Government of India Act, 1935
q.x: Fundamental Rights draw mainly on the US Bill of Rights.

q.s: The Right to Freedom of Religion in the Indian Constitution is covered by Articles:
q.x: Articles 25-28 form the Right to Freedom of Religion; 23-24 are the Right against Exploitation.

q.s: Which of the following Articles is NOT part of the Right to Freedom of Religion?
q.x: Article 29 is a cultural and educational right.

q.s: Part III (Fundamental Rights) of the Indian Constitution draws mainly on the:
q.x: The Fundamental Rights are modelled mainly on the US Bill of Rights; Britain has no written chapter of rights.

q.s: Which Article of the Constitution prohibits the employment of children below 14 years in factories, mines or hazardous employment?
q.x: Article 24 bars child labour in hazardous employment.

q.s: Which of the following Article-content pairs relating to exploitation and children is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 23 - Ban on traffic in human beings
Article 15(3) - Special provisions for women and children
Article 24 - No child below 14 in hazardous employment
q.x: Article 39(e) protects the tender age of children from abuse; free education is Article 21A.

q.s: A constitutional amendment affecting the federal provisions needs ratification by the legislatures of at least:
q.x: Under Article 368(2), federal provisions need ratification by half of the State legislatures.

q.s: In Rajendra N. Shah (2021), the Supreme Court struck down, as regards State co-operatives, the Part of the Constitution numbered:
q.x: Part IXB (97th Amendment) was struck down for State co-operatives for want of State ratification.

q.s: In which case did the Supreme Court strike down clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368, holding that limited amending power is a basic feature?
q.x: Minerva Mills (1980) invalidated the 42nd Amendment's clauses (4) and (5) of Article 368.

q.s: The India-Bangladesh Land Boundary Agreement, exchanging enclaves, was given effect by which Constitutional Amendment?
q.x: The 100th Amendment (2015) gave effect to the LBA: 111 Indian enclaves went to Bangladesh and 51 came to India.

q.s: Ceding Indian territory to a foreign State requires:
o: An ordinary law of Parliament under Article 3
A Rajya Sabha resolution under Article 249
q.x: Article 3 does not cover cession; it needs an Article 368 amendment (Berubari case).

q.s: Under which Article does the President declare assent to, or withhold assent from, a State Bill reserved by the Governor?
q.x: Article 201 deals with Bills reserved for the President; Article 200 with the Governor's assent.

q.s: Which of the following options is NOT available to a Governor with respect to a State Bill?
q.x: The Governor has no pocket veto.

q.s: 'Cabinet dictatorship' under a large majority is regarded as a demerit of the:
q.x: Cabinet dictatorship is a demerit of parliamentary government; executive-legislature deadlock belongs to the presidential system.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a demerit of the parliamentary system?
o: Absence of strict separation of powers
q.x: Deadlock between executive and legislature is a demerit of the presidential system.

q.s: The salaries of Supreme Court judges cannot be reduced after their appointment except during a:
q.x: Salaries can be cut only during a Financial Emergency under Article 360.

q.s: The form of oath of a Supreme Court judge is set out in which Schedule of the Constitution?
q.x: Oaths and affirmations are in the Third Schedule.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the emergency provisions of the Constitution is correct?
o: The Union assumes full legislative control only during a Financial Emergency.
During an emergency the federal structure turns unitary without a formal amendment.
A National Emergency can be declared only for the whole of India.
State Legislatures stand dissolved during a National Emergency.
q.x: The federal system becomes unitary in an emergency without amendment; since the 42nd Amendment a National Emergency may cover part of India.

q.s: Who is the only woman to have served as Chief Election Commissioner of India?
q.x: V.S. Ramadevi was CEC in 1990 and later Governor of Karnataka and Himachal Pradesh.

q.s: The introduction of the Elector's Photo Identity Card (EPIC) in 1993 is associated with Chief Election Commissioner:
q.x: T.N. Seshan enforced the Model Code strictly and introduced EPIC.

q.s: A member of a State Public Service Commission, though appointed by the Governor, can be removed only by the:
q.x: Only the President can remove a State PSC member; removal for misbehaviour needs a Supreme Court inquiry.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Public Service Commissions is correct?
o: A State PSC member can be removed by the Governor.
A UPSC member holds office for six years or until 65, whichever is earlier.
Removal for misbehaviour needs an inquiry by the High Court.
UPSC members are appointed by the Prime Minister.
q.x: Removal is by the President after a Supreme Court inquiry; members are appointed by the President.

q.s: The Finance Commission of India consists of a Chairman and how many other members?
q.x: Under Article 280 it has a Chairman and four members; Parliament decides their qualifications.

q.s: Members of the National Commission for Backward Classes are appointed by the:
q.x: NCBC members are appointed by the President by warrant.

q.s: Universal Children's Day, observed on 20 November, marks the adoption of the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child in:
q.x: The UNCRC was adopted on 20 November 1989.

q.s: Human Rights Day is observed every year on:
q.x: Human Rights Day (10 December) marks the adoption of the UDHR in 1948.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the National Human Rights Commission is correct?
o: It can inquire into complaints solely against private individuals.
It may intervene in court proceedings without the court's approval.
Since 2006 it may visit jails without intimating the State Government.
It can inquire into a violation only on a court's order.
q.x: It may act suo motu, on petition or on a court's order, and may intervene in court cases only with the court's approval.

q.s: In Vineet Narain v. Union of India, the Supreme Court gave superintendence over the CBI to the:
q.x: The judgment gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI and struck down the 'Single Directive'.

q.s: Which of the following statements about Vineet Narain v. Union of India is correct?
o: It placed the CBI under the Lokpal.
It held that the CBI alone decides whether a case is to be investigated.
q.x: Decided in 1997, it struck down the Single Directive and gave the CVC superintendence over the CBI.

q.s: The Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018 made bribe-giving a direct offence punishable with imprisonment up to:
q.x: Bribe-giving became an offence punishable up to 7 years; commercial organisations were also made liable.

q.s: Which of the following was NOT a change made by the Prevention of Corruption (Amendment) Act, 2018?
o: Abolition of prior approval for probing public servants
Alignment of the law with UNCAC
q.x: The 2018 Act in fact added Section 17A, requiring prior approval to investigate public servants.

q.s: During a National Emergency, Parliament can make laws on State List subjects under Article:
q.x: Article 250 gives the legislative effect; Article 353 the executive and Article 354 the financial effect.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an effect of a proclamation of National Emergency?
o: The Union can give executive directions to the States
The President can modify the distribution of revenues
Parliament can legislate on State List subjects
q.x: State Legislatures are not dissolved; Articles 250, 353 and 354 give the legislative, executive and financial effects.

q.s: Under Article 262(2), Parliament may by law exclude the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court over:
q.x: Article 262 covers inter-State river water disputes; such disputes are kept out of Article 131.

q.s: Under the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, an aggrieved State first requests the:
q.x: Under Section 3 the State asks the Central Government to refer the dispute to a tribunal.

q.s: Under the National Food Security Act, 2013, each eligible person is entitled to how much foodgrain per month?
q.x: NFSA gives 5 kg per person per month to up to 75% rural and 50% urban population.

q.s: MGNREGA (2005) guaranteed how many days of wage employment per rural household in a year?
q.x: MGNREGA guaranteed 100 days of work per household.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an effect of coalition politics in India?
o: A greater role for regional parties
A move towards a two-party system
The need to consult coalition partners
The Prime Minister becoming 'primus inter pares'
q.x: Coalitions strengthened multi-party politics, not a two-party system.

q.s: A party can be recognised as a State party, without winning any seat, by securing at least what share of the valid votes in the State?
q.x: The vote-only route needs 8% of valid votes; the 6% routes also need seats.

q.s: Under Article 243Y, the finances of Municipalities are reviewed by the:
q.x: The same State Finance Commission set up under Article 243I reviews municipal finances.

q.s: The State Election Commissioner, who conducts Panchayat elections, is appointed by the:
q.x: The Governor appoints the State Election Commissioner (Article 243K).

q.s: The State Election Commissioner can be removed only in the manner and on the grounds of a:
q.x: He is removable only like a High Court Judge.

q.s: The State Election Commission of Andhra Pradesh does NOT conduct elections to:
q.x: The SEC conducts local-body elections but not co-operative society elections.

q.s: Which of the following is a discretionary, not an obligatory, function of a Gram Panchayat in Andhra Pradesh?
q.x: Libraries and tree planting are discretionary; sanitation, water and lighting are obligatory.

q.s: The Forest Rights Act, 2006 came into force on:
q.x: It came into force on 31 December 2007.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Forest Rights Act, 2006 is correct?
o: It came into force on 1 January 2009.
It was first passed by the Rajya Sabha.
Its nodal Ministry is the Ministry of Tribal Affairs.
It does not override other laws inconsistent with it.
q.x: Tribal Affairs is the nodal Ministry; the Lok Sabha passed it first and it overrides inconsistent laws.

q.s: Under Article 243U, after the dissolution of a municipality, a fresh election must be completed within:
q.x: An election must be held within six months of dissolution.

q.s: The tax reforms in India after 1991 followed the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Raja Chelliah Committee recommended the tax reforms.

q.s: Deregulation of interest rates after 1991 followed the recommendations of the:
q.x: The Narasimham Committee led banking reforms; Tarapore dealt with capital account convertibility.

q.s: Telecom disputes and appeals in India are adjudicated by the:
q.x: TDSAT (2000) hears telecom disputes and appeals, as well as IT Act appeals.

q.s: Which of the following statements about telecom regulation is correct?
o: TRAI adjudicates telecom disputes and appeals.
TDSAT also hears appeals under the IT Act, 2000.
TDSAT was created by a separate TDSAT Act, 2000.
q.x: TDSAT was created by the 2000 amendment to the TRAI Act and also hears IT Act and DPDP Act appeals.

q.s: The Doha Development Agenda was launched at the WTO Ministerial Conference at Doha in:
q.x: MC4 at Doha (2001) launched the Doha Development Agenda.

q.s: Which of the following WTO Ministerial Conference-outcome pairs is NOT correctly matched?
o: Nairobi, 2015 - Launch of the Doha Round
Hong Kong, 2005 - Duty-free quota-free access for LDCs
q.x: Nairobi agreed to eliminate agricultural export subsidies; the Doha Round was launched in 2001.

q.s: Under the Annapurna component of NSAP, needy elderly persons receive free foodgrains of:
q.x: Annapurna gives 10 kg of free foodgrains a month to needy elderly not on IGNOAPS.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT a component of the National Social Assistance Programme?
q.x: PM-KISAN is an income-support scheme for farmers, not part of NSAP.

q.s: Which of the following statements about rural development programmes is correct?
o: IRDP was extended to the whole country on 2 October 1980.
The Desert Development Programme was launched in 1990.
The Desert Development Programme covers only hot deserts.
IRDP was launched in the First Five Year Plan.
q.x: IRDP went nationwide on 2 October 1980; the DDP (1977-78) covers both hot and cold deserts.

q.s: The slogan 'Garibi Hatao' was first introduced in planning with the:
q.x: Garibi Hatao entered planning with the Fifth Plan (1974-79).

q.s: Which of the following was NOT one of the Navaratnalu of the Andhra Pradesh Government (2019-24)?
q.x: Vahana Mitra was a separate scheme; prohibition in phases was one of the nine pillars.

q.s: The Economic Survey of India is prepared by the Economic Division of the:
q.x: It is prepared in the Department of Economic Affairs under the Chief Economic Adviser.

q.s: The first Economic Survey of India was presented for the year:
q.x: The first Survey was for 1950-51; it has been separate from the Budget since 1964.

q.s: The Economic Survey 2025-26 raised India's potential growth estimate to:
q.x: The Survey, tabled on 29 January 2026, put potential growth at 7%.

q.s: The term 'jobless growth' was coined by:
q.x: Nick Perna coined the term 'jobless growth'.

q.s: Employment elasticity is calculated as:
o: Change in labour force / change in population
% change in output / % change in employment
% change in employment / % change in output
q.x: A low elasticity means output grows with little rise in employment.

q.s: The Quarterly Employment Survey (QES) in India is conducted by the:
q.x: The Labour Bureau conducts the QES, which covers nine non-farm sectors.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Quarterly Employment Survey is correct?
o: It covers only the public sector.
Manufacturing is its largest employer, followed by education.
Agriculture is one of its nine sectors.
It is conducted by the NSO.
q.x: Manufacturing leads, followed by education; it covers non-farm establishments with 10 or more workers.

q.s: In W.W. Rostow's stages of economic growth, which stage comes immediately after the 'take-off'?
q.x: The order is traditional society, pre-conditions, take-off, drive to maturity and high mass consumption.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT one of W.W. Rostow's stages of economic growth?
q.x: The 'big push' is Rosenstein-Rodan's theory.

q.s: Article 31C of the Constitution was inserted by the:
q.x: The 25th Amendment (1971) inserted Article 31C.

q.s: Clause (2) of Article 38, directing the State to minimise inequalities in income, was added by the:
q.x: Article 38(2) came with the 44th Amendment, 1978.

q.s: In a Lorenz curve diagram, the 45-degree diagonal line represents:
q.x: The diagonal is the line of perfect equality; the farther the curve bows away, the greater the inequality.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the Lorenz curve is correct?
o: The X-axis shows the cumulative percentage of population, poorest first.
The farther the curve bows away, the lower the inequality.
It gives a single numerical measure of inequality.
q.x: The Gini coefficient, not the curve, gives the number; the diagonal is perfect equality.

q.s: India moved from a centralised (imperative-type) approach towards indicative planning from the:
q.x: Indicative planning began with the Eighth Plan (1992-97); Stalin's USSR and China are examples of imperative planning.

q.s: Which of the following is NOT an example of imperative planning?
q.x: India moved towards indicative planning from the Eighth Plan.

q.s: During the Eleventh Five Year Plan, which sector received the first priority in Andhra Pradesh's plan?
q.x: The social sector, not industry, got first priority; agriculture was about 21.27% of GSDP.

q.s: The terms of reference of the Fifteenth Finance Commission mandated the use of population figures of the:
q.x: The 2011 Census base was mandated; the southern States objected to it.

q.s: The terms of reference of the Fifteenth Finance Commission included a non-lapsable fund for:
q.x: It was asked to consider a non-lapsable fund for defence and internal security.

q.s: Which of the following is an entry condition for local bodies to receive grants under the 16th Finance Commission?
q.x: Online audited accounts and a timely State Finance Commission are entry conditions; municipal bonds are not.

q.s: Which States topped NITI Aayog's SDG India Index 2023-24 with a score of 79?
q.x: Kerala and Uttarakhand shared the top spot; India's composite score rose to 71.

q.s: Which of the following statements about the SDG India Index 2023-24 is correct?
